headline: Microsoft issues emergency Windows 11 update to fix September patch bugs
summary: An out-of-band update addresses issues with Remote Desktop, USB audio, and Hyper-V after the record-breaking September patch.
details: Microsoft has released an emergency out-of-band update to resolve problems introduced by its September Patch Tuesday update. This update specifically targets issues affecting Remote Desktop Services, certain USB audio devices, and folder shares on Hyper-V-based Linux virtual machines.

The September patch was Microsoft's largest ever, aiming to fix nearly 1,000 vulnerabilities. However, it inadvertently caused disruptions for businesses, developers, and gamers, necessitating this rapid, unscheduled fix.

This out-of-band update is now available for Windows 11 versions 26H2, 25H2, and 24H2. Microsoft has also extended these fixes to various Windows Server versions, including Server 2025 and 2022, as well as LTSC versions of Windows 10 and older server editions.

The frequency of out-of-band updates from Microsoft has increased significantly this year, indicating a growing challenge in ensuring the stability of its major patches. Previous instances this year required multiple emergency updates to address installation failures, sign-in problems, and even Intel driver issues causing performance degradation.
caption:
Microsoft issues emergency Windows 11 update to fix bugs introduced by its massive September patch.

Microsoft has released an emergency out-of-band update to resolve problems introduced by its September Patch Tuesday update. This update specifically targets issues affecting Remote Desktop Services, certain USB audio devices, and folder shares on Hyper-V-based Linux virtual machines.

The September patch was Microsoft's largest ever, aiming to fix nearly 1,000 vulnerabilities. However, it inadvertently caused disruptions for businesses, developers, and gamers, necessitating this rapid, unscheduled fix.

This out-of-band update is now available for Windows 11 versions 26H2, 25H2, and 24H2. Microsoft has also extended these fixes to various Windows Server versions, including Server 2025 and 2022, as well as LTSC versions of Windows 10 and older server editions.

The frequency of out-of-band updates from Microsoft has increased significantly this year, indicating a growing challenge in ensuring the stability of its major patches. Previous instances this year required multiple emergency updates to address installation failures, sign-in problems, and even Intel driver issues causing performance degradation.
